conventions: TypeScript strict; no `any`, no non-null assertions on values that can legitimately be missing; arrow-function `const` declarations as in lasso/utils.ts.
Formatting is Prettier through eslint-plugin-prettier (80 columns, double quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent, semicolons); `curly` is enforced, so every if-body has braces.

Import order (eslint import/order): external packages, then `@excalidraw/**` packages, then parent (`../`), then sibling (`./`), then type-only imports last; a blank line between groups; type-only imports use separate `import type { ... }` statements.
Reuse only helpers already exported by `@excalidraw/math` and `@excalidraw/element`; no new dependency and no new file.
`"contain"` is the Wrap mode and `"overlap"` is the Overlap mode of `AppState["boxSelectionMode"]`; never introduce another name or setting for them.
Never edit or import-for-edit the off-limits files (App.tsx, appState.ts, types.ts, restore.ts, packages/element/src/**); importing a type from `../types` is allowed.

Tests run on vitest with jsdom and globals (`describe`, `it`, `expect`, `beforeEach`); use `window.h`, the `API` helper (`./helpers/api`), the `Pointer` helper and `assertSelectedElements` as the surrounding file does.
Tests never add, update or rely on a snapshot (`toMatchSnapshot` is forbidden in new cases); no `__snapshots__` file may change.
No user-facing text, locale key or UI change.

decisions.choice: A required field `boxSelectionMode: AppState["boxSelectionMode"]` on the existing input object; both callers (lasso/index.ts and tests/lasso.test.tsx) pass it explicitly.
decisions.reason: Only two callers exist and both change in this run; a required field makes the compiler catch any caller that forgets the mode.

decisions.choice: Exactly today's code path: AABB pre-filter with doBoundsIntersect, then enclosureTest (any outline point inside) else intersectionTest (lasso crosses outline or bound-text label).
rejected: rewriting Overlap on top of the new containment helper
decisions.reason: FR-2 and AC-5 require today's behaviour bit for bit, and existing lasso tests pin it.

decisions.choice: An element is enclosed when (1) its getElementBounds AABB is inside the lasso AABB (boundsContainBounds, cheap early reject), (2) every point of every segment in elementsSegments.get(id) is inside the lasso polygon (polygonIncludesPointNonZero), (3) every outline point of its positioned bound-text label is inside too, and (4) intersectionTest(path, element, elementsMap) is false (no lasso edge crosses the outline or the label).
rejected: AABB-only containment as box selection does
decisions.reason: Sampled-point containment plus the crossing test is exact for straight outlines and catches a lasso that cuts a curve between samples (FR-4), stays O(points x lasso segments) (NFR-3) and reuses existing helpers (NFR-2).

decisions.choice: In "contain" mode an element for which isBoundToContainer(element) is true is skipped; its label is judged only as part of its container. In "overlap" mode bound text is evaluated as today.
rejected: evaluating the label on its own in Wrap
skipping bound text in both modes
decisions.reason: Mirrors box selection (shouldIgnoreElementFromSelection ignores bound text) so a label poking outside the lasso cannot select its container through the text-to-container mapping in LassoTrail; Overlap must stay unchanged (FR-7).

decisions.topic: Where the live mode is read
decisions.choice: LassoTrail.updateSelection passes `this.app.state.boxSelectionMode` on every call; nothing is cached on the LassoTrail instance.
decisions.reason: FR-6: a preference change applies to the next stroke without reload.

decisions.topic: Mode selection in the util-level tests
decisions.choice: tests/lasso.test.tsx `updatePath` takes a required third argument `mode: AppState["boxSelectionMode"]`, sets `h.setState({ boxSelectionMode: mode })` before drawing so the LassoTrail's own selection agrees, and passes the same mode to getLassoSelectedElementIds; every existing call passes "overlap".
decisions.reason: Assumption 2 of requirements: existing tests keep their expectations and run with "overlap" passed explicitly.

decisions.topic: Mode selection in the pointer-driven tests
decisions.choice: tests/selection.test.tsx renders `<Excalidraw />` and sets the mode with `API.setAppState({ boxSelectionMode })` before each stroke; the lasso is drawn with the existing `mouse` Pointer (downAt, moveTo, up) after `h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "lasso" })` inside act.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for tests through the lasso tool; setAppState lets one test switch the mode between strokes (FR-6).

units.behaviour: getLassoSelectedElementIds takes a required boxSelectionMode and, in "contain" (Wrap), selects only elements (with their bound-text label) fully enclosed by the lasso; "overlap" keeps today's enclose-or-intersect path unchanged.
rules: 1. The input object gains the required field `boxSelectionMode: AppState["boxSelectionMode"]`, destructured with the other fields; the return shape `{ selectedElementIds }` is unchanged.
2. Path simplification, the unlocked filter, the clearing of both sets and the lassoBounds reduce stay exactly as they are.
3. In the loop, when boxSelectionMode === "contain" and isBoundToContainer(element) is true, `continue` before any other work (the label is judged as part of its container).
4. elementBounds and the existing guard (doBoundsIntersect(lassoBounds, elementBounds) and not already in either set) stay as they are.

5. Inside the guard, when boxSelectionMode === "contain": if containmentTest(path, element, elementBounds, lassoBounds, elementsMap, elementsSegments) is true add element.id to enclosedElements; never add to intersectedElements in this mode.
6. Otherwise ("overlap") run today's code verbatim: enclosureTest, else intersectionTest, adding to enclosedElements / intersectedElements as now.

7. New module-private `const containmentTest = (lassoPath: GlobalPoint[], element: ExcalidrawElement, elementBounds: Bounds, lassoBounds: Bounds, elementsMap: ElementsMap, elementsSegments: ElementsSegmentsMap): boolean`, placed right after enclosureTest.
8. containmentTest step 1: return false when !boundsContainBounds(lassoBounds, elementBounds) (cheap AABB early reject).
9. containmentTest step 2: segments = elementsSegments.get(element.id); return false when it is missing or empty.
10. containmentTest step 3: lassoPolygon = polygonFromPoints(lassoPath); return false unless every point of every segment satisfies polygonIncludesPointNonZero(point, lassoPolygon).

11. containmentTest step 4: boundTextElement = getBoundTextElement(element, elementsMap); when present, compute getElementLineSegments({ ...boundTextElement, ...computeBoundTextPosition(element, boundTextElement, elementsMap) }, elementsMap) and return false unless every point of every label segment is inside lassoPolygon.
12. containmentTest step 5: return !intersectionTest(lassoPath, element, elementsMap) (a lasso edge crossing the outline or the label, including between curve samples, rejects the element).
13. enclosureTest and intersectionTest bodies are not changed.

14. Helper signatures from @excalidraw/element: boundsContainBounds(outerBounds: Bounds, innerBounds: Bounds): boolean (inclusive corners check); getElementLineSegments(element: ExcalidrawElement, elementsMap: ElementsMap): LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[] (rotation already applied); isBoundToContainer(element: ExcalidrawElement | null): boolean.

units.behaviour: updatePath takes the selection mode; every existing case passes "overlap" with unchanged expectations, and a new describe covers Wrap vs Overlap per shape and for bound text.
rules: 1. updatePath signature becomes `(startPoint: GlobalPoint, points: LocalPoint[], mode: AppState["boxSelectionMode"])`; first statement inside its outer act is `h.setState({ boxSelectionMode: mode });`, and getLassoSelectedElementIds receives `boxSelectionMode: mode`.
2. The six existing updatePath calls pass "overlap" as the third argument; no existing expectation changes.

3. New `describe("Lasso selection modes (Wrap / Overlap)", ...)` appended at the end of the file; it relies on the file-level beforeEach render and builds elements with API.createElement and API.setElements.

4. Inside it define `const lassoBox = (x1: number, y1: number, x2: number, y2: number, mode: AppState["boxSelectionMode"]) =>` calling updatePath(pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(x1, y1), [[0, 0], [x2 - x1, 0], [x2 - x1, y2 - y1], [0, y2 - y1], [0, 0]] as LocalPoint[], mode).
5. Inside it define `const selectedIds = () => getSelectedElements(h.elements, h.state).map((element) => element.id);` and assert with `expect(selectedIds()).toEqual([...])`.
6. Each it() covers one shape and runs its lassos in both modes in sequence; API.setElements is called once per it(), since each lassoBox starts a fresh path that clears the previous selection.
7. No snapshot assertions.

rules: 1. New `describe("lasso selection modes", ...)` inserted right after the "lasso reselection" describe; its beforeEach is `await render(<Excalidraw />);`.

2. Inside it define `const lassoBox = (x1: number, y1: number, x2: number, y2: number) =>` that runs `act(() => { h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "lasso" }); });` then mouse.downAt(x1, y1), mouse.moveTo(x2, y1), mouse.moveTo(x2, y2), mouse.moveTo(x1, y2), mouse.moveTo(x1, y1), mouse.up().
3. Set the mode before each stroke with `API.setAppState({ boxSelectionMode: "contain" })` or `"overlap"`; call API.clearSelection() between two strokes in the same case.
